analysis: Examined the SSDHybridCheckpointStore+Maintenance.swift patch and the docs/reference/ssd-kv-cache.md update. The code change splits removeCorrupt into removeFile plus a corruptDropped counter increment. In scanOnDisk, a checkpoint whose mtime is past the TTL is now removed through removeFile (the same performIndexedRemoval path: removeItemIfSafe plus index.remove) instead of being counted as corrupt. The other validity predicates (magic, metadata, blockSize, lookupTag prefix match, size/date attributes) still route to removeCorrupt. Security effect: no loosening of TTL enforcement, because an expired file is still unlinked and never indexed, so the T-041 30-minute TTL bound and at-rest cleanup are preserved. There is no new authentication, encryption or identity-binding path. Removal still runs under performIndexedRemoval, which per the docs is serialized by removalLock and refused when the store is closed or does not own its epoch. The only behavioral difference is telemetry: corrupt_drops_total no longer includes TTL-expired files. That reduces noise and does not hide corruption, since parse and auth failures are still counted. Epoch handling is unchanged: per-file removals do not rotate the epoch, consistent with the T-041 sign-off. The docs change (lines 88-91) matches the code and is a documentation date bump plus a clarifying sentence. Remaining uncertainty is limited to the unchanged parts of scanOnDisk, which were not supplied; I saw no issue in the changed lines.
